request_context: A request to attack the decisions and trade-offs of a design document as a skeptical reviewer, with findings sorted by how serious they are.

rules.source_quote: N CRITICAL (architectural), N CRITICAL (factual), N IMPORTANT, N SUGGESTION
rules.outcome: Ends with a count of findings in each severity class.

rules.source_quote: Wrong architecture choice for the stated requirements
rules.outcome: Rates a design that contradicts a stated requirement (a synchronous call where the requirement says async) as CRITICAL architectural.
rules.why: A design that breaks its own requirement cannot ship.
rules.scenario_hint: A sync design for an async requirement.

rules.source_quote: Missing security boundary (no auth, no encryption at rest/transit where PII is involved)
rules.outcome: Rates personal data handled with no stated encryption or access control as CRITICAL architectural.
rules.why: Missing boundaries on PII are launch blockers.
rules.scenario_hint: A design storing personal data with no encryption stated.

rules.source_quote: Single point of failure with no stated mitigation
rules.outcome: Rates a single component whose loss stops the system, with no mitigation stated, as CRITICAL architectural.
rules.why: Unmitigated single points break availability goals.
rules.scenario_hint: One instance or one region with no failover.

rules.source_quote: Incorrect technical claim about a service or technology
rules.outcome: Rates a false claim about a service (a wrong limit, a feature that does not exist) as CRITICAL factual.
rules.why: False facts make the design not work.
rules.scenario_hint: A doc citing a wrong service limit.

rules.source_quote: Contradictory requirements (two requirements that cannot both be satisfied)
rules.outcome: Rates two requirements that cannot both hold as CRITICAL factual and names both.
rules.scenario_hint: Requirements for strong consistency and no cross-region latency at once.

rules.source_quote: Missing alternative in a decision that has obvious alternatives
rules.outcome: Rates a significant decision with no alternatives considered, or an obvious alternative left out, as IMPORTANT.
rules.why: A choice with no alternatives cannot be judged.
rules.scenario_hint: An ADR naming one option only.

rules.source_quote: Incomplete trade-off (dimensions missing: cost, latency, complexity, scalability, operability)
rules.outcome: Rates a trade-off that leaves out key dimensions as IMPORTANT and names the missing ones.
rules.scenario_hint: A trade-off table with only cost and latency.

rules.source_quote: Flag any identified fallacy as IMPORTANT with the fallacy name and the affected section.
rules.outcome: Names the fallacy in a justification (false dichotomy, circular reasoning, appeal to authority) and rates it IMPORTANT.
rules.scenario_hint: A justification that cites a big company as proof.

rules.source_quote: Do not raise a CRITICAL because a design looks risky.
rules.outcome: Keeps unsourced load figures and unproven dependencies at IMPORTANT, and saves CRITICAL for broken requirements, missing required boundaries, unmitigated single points and false facts.

rules.source_quote: Name the requirement (e.g., R2) the finding breaks.
rules.outcome: Each CRITICAL finding names the requirement it breaks by its label.

rules.source_quote: Do not add requirements, regulations, services, or numbers the document does not state
rules.outcome: Does not invent requirements, laws or numbers the doc does not state, and adds no generic checklist items with no anchor in the text.
rules.scenario_hint: A doc with no regulatory scope.

rules.source_quote: Every finding, SUGGESTION included, gets a concrete `Rebuttal needed` line
rules.outcome: Each finding says what evidence, alternative or change would answer it.
rules.why: Authors need a way to close each finding.

rules.source_quote: the document does not advance to PE review with any CRITICAL finding present
rules.outcome: Says the doc does not advance while any CRITICAL finding stands, and states the advance condition.

rules.source_quote: HIGH requires multi-axis corroboration and is unavailable when the panel is declined
rules.outcome: In a single-voice review (no panel), gives no finding HIGH confidence and says the review was single-voice.
rules.why: Confidence must match how the review was done.
rules.scenario_hint: A user asking for a quick single pass.

rules.source_quote: Every finding cites the section and the text it challenges.
rules.outcome: Each finding points to the section it challenges.
rules.why: Any good review points to the place.

rules.source_quote: When a finding relies on outside knowledge (a service limit, a pricing figure), say so in the challenge.
rules.outcome: Says when a challenge rests on outside knowledge, such as a service limit, rather than on the doc.
rules.why: Authors can check the outside fact.
rules.scenario_hint: A finding about a service limit the doc does not state.
